The slide features a large, centered diagram on a plain white background. At the top-left, the title 'Introduction' is written in a simple, black sans-serif font. The central visual is a colorful contour map with purple, teal, and yellow gradients, overlaid with small white arrows representing a vector field. Along this path, five white circular markers are placed, each linked by a thin gray callout line to a small rectangular photograph of a house. These houses show a visual progression from a simple, weathered wooden shack at the start to a more modern, well-maintained red house at the end. To the right of the central diagram, there is a large, bright green checkmark icon. The overall text density is very light, focusing primarily on the visual representation of a concept, likely related to latent space interpolation or optimization.

The slide follows a clean, single-column layout on a plain white background. The title is located at the top-left in a large, bold, black font. The main content consists of two primary bullet points. The first bullet point, 'Length of path:', is followed by a centered integral equation for 'S'. The second bullet point, 'Riemannian Metric:', is followed by a centered block of equations defining the metric 'L' and its associated terms like 'K(gamma)'. The mathematical expressions are clearly separated from the bulleted text, creating a structured and easy-to-read presentation of foundational formulas. The overall text density is light, with ample white space surrounding the equations.

The slide uses a two-column layout with a large, bold title positioned at the top-left. The left column contains three main bullet points that organize mathematical content: 'Length of path', 'Riemannian Metric', and 'Functional derivative'. Each bullet is followed by centered mathematical equations. Notably, in the third section, a specific term in the functional derivative equation is highlighted with a red box, and an arrow points from it to the explanatory text 'Estimated by a diffusion model'. The right column features two vertically stacked figures. The top figure is a 2D contour plot with a vector field, showing a curved path (geodesic) and a straight dashed line between points A and B, with a yellow arrow pointing to the geodesic. The bottom figure is a 1D line plot showing a dashed curve being transformed into a solid, multi-modal curve, also indicated by a yellow arrow. The slide has a white background and a moderate density of information, balancing text, equations, and illustrative graphics.

layout_structure.title_text: Geodesics in the Diffusion Latent Space
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide follows a clean, single-column layout on a plain white background. The title is positioned at the top left in a large, bold, sans-serif font. Below the title, there is a section of text organized into a hierarchical bulleted list with two levels. The primary bullet point is 'Image Interpolation:', followed by three sub-bullets that define the problem as a boundary value problem with two images as input and a geodesic trajectory as output. The bottom portion of the slide features a horizontal row of five square images depicting a smooth visual transition (interpolation) between two different cat faces. Small blue arrows are placed between the first and second images, and between the fourth and fifth images, pointing inward to suggest a process of moving from the endpoints toward the center. The text density is light, with the visual sequence of images serving as the primary focus to illustrate the concept.

layout_structure.layout_description: The slide follows a clean, minimalist layout. A large, bold title 'Video Analysis' is positioned at the top-left. Directly below it, a single grey bullet point introduces a line of text: 'Test whether short video clips are approximately geodesic.' The central and lower portion of the slide is occupied by four square images arranged in a single horizontal row. These images appear to be frames from video clips, each showing a different 3D rendered object on a plain grey surface: a red cube, a teal cylinder, a dark grey cube, and a lime green sphere. The background of the slide is plain white, and the overall text density is light, emphasizing the visual content.

The slide features a large, bold title 'Video Analysis' positioned at the top-left. The main content area is organized into two columns. On the left, there is a small, square-format image showing a pink cube on a plain, light-colored surface. To the right of this image is a large line graph that occupies most of the slide's width. The graph displays four jagged lines in different colors (pink, yellow-green, green, and light blue) plotted over a time axis 't' ranging from 0 to 1. The y-axis is labeled with a mathematical norm expression and includes a scale factor of 10^-5. A legend is located in the top-right corner of the graph area, identifying the four data series. The slide has a clean white background with very light text density, prioritizing visual data over textual explanation.

The slide features a minimalist design with a plain white background. A single-line title in a sans-serif font is positioned at the top-left. The primary content is organized into two vertical columns of small, square images located at the far left and far right margins of the slide. The left column contains four images: a man's portrait, a crashing ocean wave, a cat's face, and a stack of pancakes. The right column contains four corresponding images: a different man's portrait, a stylized wave painting, a dog's face, and a burger. A large, empty white space occupies the center of the slide between these two columns, intended to showcase the results of image interpolation between the source images on the left and the target images on the right. The text density is very light, with no bullet points, equations, or additional labels.

The slide follows a clean grid layout on a plain white background. A large, black, sans-serif title is aligned to the top-left. The central content is a dense grid of images arranged in four rows and eleven columns, illustrating qualitative results of image interpolation. Each row represents a different transformation sequence: the first row shows a man morphing from an older to a younger appearance; the second row transitions from a realistic photo of a wave to a famous Japanese woodblock print; the third row shows a cat morphing into a dog; and the fourth row shows a stack of pancakes transforming into a burger. There are no bullet points, equations, or other text elements, resulting in a very light text density where the focus is entirely on the visual transitions.
